changes.before: The horse has no horns; with horns it would spare no one.
changes.after: By design, the horse has no horns; with horns it would spare no one.
changes.reason: Carry the opening knowing/intending force contextually, without adding a named agent.

changes.before: The supplied gloss invokes divine restraint; this is the collection’s explanation, not evidence for a particular myth or author. The last clause’s omitted object is rendered “no one” in English in line with the gloss’s reference to heeding nobody. The opening ଜାଣି does not securely establish who knows or intends this; the English does not turn it into an imperative. Its agency remains unresolved.
changes.after: The supplied gloss imagines divine restraint on the strong. “By design” carries that contextual reading of ଜାଣି without naming an agent in the verse. The final clause leaves its object unstated; “no one” follows the gloss’s reference to heeding nobody.
changes.reason: Explain supported contextual choices plainly; retain actual elliptical limits without presenting them as a failed translation.
